Reproducing Peterson et al. (2021) from DANDI:000055¶

Paper: Peterson, Singh, Wang, Rao and Brunton (2021), "Behavioral and Neural Variability of Naturalistic Arm Movements", eNeuro 8(3), ENEURO.0007-21.2021, doi:10.1523/eneuro.0007-21.2021.

Dataset: DANDI:000055 (AJILE12), version 0.261123.1703 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000055/0.261123.1703). This version was asked for in the prompt of this attempt, a repeat attempt that tests what the dataset holds now. It holds 55 NWB files, one per subject and recording day, with ECoG at 500 Hz, pose at 30 Hz, the contralateral wrist movement events and their features. Every file is streamed; nothing is downloaded.

Claims: claims/peterson-2021.yaml, written from the version of record (Europe PMC, PMC8225404) and checked by a second reader. Method details the claims file does not give are taken from the paper's Methods and its code (github.com/BruntonUWBio/naturalistic_arm_movements_ecog, commit 04c6faf2f219586fa834d10c614ef48a694cec55), cited where they are used. Outside input: the paper's projection matrices from electrodes to regions, Figshare item 12114408 version 1 (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.12114408.v1).

The notebook runs for about an hour: about 10 to 13 minutes to stream the ECoG around 8088 events (about 150 GB of compressed chunks), about 35 minutes for the 3904 regression models and about 10 to 15 minutes for the regression variants. The last cell prints the time of the run.

Assumptions (the paper leaves these open; each is stated where it is used): how the segment rejection pools power over electrodes and frequencies; and that the good electrodes of a subject are those marked good in every one of its files, for the segment rejection, the region projection, the regression and the electrode-level analyses (the claims file's opening comment renormalises the weights per subject). For the region claims two other electrode choices are shown as variants: the flags of each event's own file, and the electrodes good in at least one file of the subject. The paper's count of removed electrodes favours each file's own flags (section "Region results under other electrode choices"), and the outcome of fig5-recording-day-effects rests on them: partially reproduced, where the main set would give not reproduced.

# Checks of the description against the values
m0 = metas[0]
print("ECoG unit:", m0["ecog_unit"], "conversion:", m0["ecog_conversion"], "rate:", m0["ecog_rate"], "start:", m0["ecog_start"],
      "chunks:", m0["ecog_chunks"])
print("pose unit:", m0["pose_unit"], "rate:", m0["pose_rate"], "series:", m0["pose_series"])
print("all ECoG at 500 Hz:", all(m["ecog_rate"] == 500 for m in metas), "; all pose at 30 Hz:", all(m["pose_rate"] == 30 for m in metas))
print("ElectricalSeries rows = electrodes table:", all(m["ecog_shape"][1] == len(m["electrodes"]) and
      np.array_equal(m["es_electrodes"], np.arange(len(m["electrodes"]))) for m in metas))
print("ReachEvents timestamps = reaches start_time (max diff, s):",
      max(np.abs(m["event_times"] - m["reaches"].start_time.values).max() for m in metas))
for m in metas:
    d = np.abs(m["event_times"] - m["reaches"].start_time.values)
    if (d > 1).any():
        k = np.flatnonzero(d > 1)
        print(f"  S{int(m['subject_id']):02d} day {m['session_id']}: {len(k)} event(s) differ by more than 1 s; ReachEvents",
              m["event_times"][k].round(1), "s, start_time", m["reaches"].start_time.values[k].round(1), "s; ECoG length",
              m["ecog_shape"][0] / m["ecog_rate"], "s")
print("events differing by more than 1 s, all files:",
      sum(int((np.abs(m["event_times"] - m["reaches"].start_time.values) > 1).sum()) for m in metas))
# electrode positions and flags across a subject's files
for s in subjects:
    ms = [m for m in metas if int(m["subject_id"]) == s]
    xyz = [m["electrodes"][["x", "y", "z"]].values for m in ms]
    same = all(np.array_equal(a, xyz[0], equal_nan=True) for a in xyz)
    G = np.array([m["electrodes"].good.values for m in ms])
    print(f"S{s:02d}: positions identical across files {same}; electrodes without position {int(np.isnan(xyz[0][:, 0]).sum())}; "
          f"bad per file {list((~G).sum(1))}; bad in every file {(~G).all(0).sum()}; bad in any file {(~G).any(0).sum()}")
# Electrodes removed per subject under three readings of the flags, against the paper's "removal of
# 4.9 +- 4.9 surface electrodes per subject and 1.0 +- 1.4 depth electrodes for each of the five subjects
# with depth electrodes" (Methods, "ECoG data processing"). Depth: groups described as depth (cohort).
rm = []
for s in subjects:
    ms = [m for m in metas if int(m["subject_id"]) == s]
    G = np.array([m["electrodes"].good.values for m in ms]).astype(bool)
    dep = ms[0]["electrodes"].group_name.map(ms[0]["groups"]).fillna("").str.contains("depth", case=False).values
    for name, bad in (("bad in any file", (~G).any(0)), ("bad in every file", (~G).all(0))):
        rm.append(dict(subject=s, reading=name, surface=int((bad & ~dep).sum()), depth=int((bad & dep).sum()), has_depth=bool(dep.any())))
    rm.append(dict(subject=s, reading="each file's flags (mean over files)", surface=float((~G[:, ~dep]).sum(1).mean()),
                   depth=float((~G[:, dep]).sum(1).mean()), has_depth=bool(dep.any())))
rm = pd.DataFrame(rm)
print("electrodes removed per subject (surface / depth):")
print(rm.pivot(index="subject", columns="reading", values=["surface", "depth"]).round(1).to_string())
for name, g in rm.groupby("reading", sort=False):
    d = g[g.has_depth].depth
    print(f"  {name}: surface {g.surface.mean():.1f} +- {g.surface.std():.1f} per subject (paper 4.9 +- 4.9); "
          f"depth {d.mean():.1f} +- {d.std():.1f} over the {len(d)} subjects with depth groups (paper 1.0 +- 1.4)")
print("columns of the reaches table:", list(metas[0]["reaches"].columns))
print("columns of the electrodes table:", list(metas[0]["electrodes"].columns))
print("columns of the epochs table:", list(metas[0]["epochs"].columns))
desc = ev_all[["duration", "magnitude", "angle_raw", "onset_speed", "speech_ratio", "Bimanual_ratio", "bimanual_overlap",
               "bimanual_class", "time_of_day"]].describe().T
print(desc)
print("missing values per reaches column:", ev_all[["Reach_magnitude_px", "Reach_angle_degrees", "Onset_speed_px_per_sec",
      "Speech_ratio", "Bimanual_ratio", "Bimanual_overlap", "Bimanual_class"]].isna().sum().to_dict())
print("bimanual_class values:", sorted(ev_all.bimanual_class.unique()))

Projection matrices (outside input) and claim roi-projection-link¶

The rows of the paper's projection matrices from electrodes to the eight regions, deposited on Figshare, can be matched one to one to the dataset's electrodes, and their weights fit the electrodes' positions.

Figshare item 12114408, version 1 (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.12114408.v1), read at run time. Rows are matched as the paper's code does (tfr_utils.load_project_spectral_power, commit 04c6faf): it keeps the non-zero rows and drops the first of them (np.nonzero(df.transpose().mean().values != 0)[0][1:]).

In [6]:
files, fig_meta = ajile.figshare_files()
print("Figshare item", fig_meta["id"], "version", fig_meta["version"], fig_meta["doi"])
proj, cents, link_rows = {}, {}, []
el_first = {s: [m for m in metas if int(m["subject_id"]) == s][0]["electrodes"] for s in subjects}
for s in subjects:
    m, c = ajile.load_projection(s, files)
    el = el_first[s]
    known = el.x.notna().values
    a, note = ajile.match_projection(m, known)
    # rule as the claims file words it: drop all-zero rows only
    allz = m.values.astype(float)
    n_nonzero = int((allz.mean(axis=1) != 0).sum())
    proj[s] = (list(m.columns), a)
    cents[s] = c
    link_rows.append(dict(subject=s, csv_rows=len(m), electrodes=len(el), with_position=int(known.sum()),
                          nonzero_rows=n_nonzero, code_rule=note, matched=a is not None))
link = pd.DataFrame(link_rows)
print(link.to_string())
cols_all = proj[1][0]
# The first non-zero row of each file, the row the code drops, holds the electrode density of each
# region (the remaining rows sum to 1 per region). Regions kept: mean density over subjects > 3 (Methods).
dens_rows = []
for s in subjects:
    m, _ = ajile.load_projection(s, files)
    a = m.values.astype(float)
    first = a[np.flatnonzero(a.mean(axis=1) != 0)[0]]
    rest = a[np.flatnonzero(a.mean(axis=1) != 0)[1:]]
    dens_rows.append(first)
    # rows after the density row, in order: are the zero rows those of the electrodes without a position?
    after = a[np.flatnonzero(a.mean(axis=1) != 0)[0] + 1:]
    zero = np.flatnonzero(after.mean(axis=1) == 0)
    nopos = np.flatnonzero(el_first[s].x.isna().values)
    n_el = len(el_first[s])
    print(f"S{s:02d}: zero rows among the first {n_el} after the density row at", list(zero[zero < n_el]),
          "; electrodes without a position at", list(nopos), "; same:", np.array_equal(zero[zero < n_el], nopos),
          "; zero rows past the last electrode:", int((zero >= n_el).sum()))
    if s == 1:
        print("S01: rows after the first sum per region to (first 6 regions):", rest.sum(axis=0)[:6].round(3))
dens = np.array(dens_rows).mean(axis=0)
print("mean density of the eight regions:", {r: round(float(dens[cols_all.index(r)]), 2) for r in ajile.ROIS})
kept = [cols_all[i] for i in np.flatnonzero(dens > 3)]
print("regions with mean density > 3:", kept)
print("same as the eight of the claims file:", sorted(kept) == sorted(ajile.ROIS))

# Largest-weight region against the nearest region centroid, with mirrored MNI positions
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed("roi-projection-link"))
def nearest_match(s, rng=None, n_shuffle=200):
    names, a = proj[s]
    c = cents[s]
    cn = [str(x) for x in c.columns]
    cent = c.values.astype(float)            # one row per AAL region, left-side centroids
    el = el_first[s]
    known = el.x.notna().values
    pos = el[["x", "y", "z"]].values[known].copy()
    pos[:, 0] = -np.abs(pos[:, 0])             # mirror to the left hemisphere
    W = a[known]
    has = W.sum(axis=1) > 0
    valid = np.isfinite(cent).all(axis=1) & (np.abs(cent).sum(axis=1) > 0)
    d = np.linalg.norm(pos[:, None, :] - cent[None, :, :], axis=2)
    d[:, ~valid] = np.inf
    near = d.argmin(axis=1)
    top = np.where(valid[None, :], W, -np.inf).argmax(axis=1)
    obs = int((near[has] == top[has]).sum())
    null = []
    for _ in range(n_shuffle):
        p = rng.permutation(len(W))
        topp = np.where(valid[None, :], W[p], -np.inf).argmax(axis=1)
        null.append(int((near[has] == topp[has]).sum()))
    return obs, int(has.sum()), np.array(null)
print("centroid table shape:", cents[1].shape, "columns:", list(cents[1].columns))
res_link = []
for s in subjects:
    obs, n, null = nearest_match(s, rng)
    res_link.append(dict(subject=s, matched_electrodes=n, top_is_nearest=obs, frac=obs / n,
                         shuffled_mean=null.mean(), shuffled_max=null.max(), beats_all_shuffles=obs > null.max()))
res_link = pd.DataFrame(res_link)
print(res_link.to_string())
# seed sensitivity
for off in SEED_OFFSETS[1:]:
    r2_ = np.random.default_rng(seed("roi-projection-link") + off)
    print("seed +", off, "subjects beating every shuffle:", sum(nearest_match(s, r2_)[0] > nearest_match(s, r2_)[2].max() for s in subjects))
# Shifted alignment: rows applied k places later or earlier (an offset the shuffle null cannot detect)
def shift_match(s, k):
    names, a = proj[s]
    c = cents[s].values.astype(float)
    el = el_first[s]
    known = el.x.notna().values
    pos = el[["x", "y", "z"]].values[known].copy()
    pos[:, 0] = -np.abs(pos[:, 0])
    W = a[known]
    valid = np.isfinite(c).all(axis=1) & (np.abs(c).sum(axis=1) > 0)
    d = np.linalg.norm(pos[:, None, :] - c[None, :, :], axis=2)
    d[:, ~valid] = np.inf
    near = d.argmin(axis=1)
    i = np.arange(len(W)); j = i + k
    ok = (j >= 0) & (j < len(W))
    Wk = W[j[ok]]
    has = Wk.sum(axis=1) > 0
    top = np.where(valid[None, :], Wk, -np.inf).argmax(axis=1)
    return float((near[i[ok]][has] == top[has]).mean())
shifts = pd.DataFrame({k: [shift_match(s, k) for s in subjects] for k in range(-3, 4)}, index=[f"S{s:02d}" for s in subjects])
print("fraction of electrodes whose largest-weight region is the nearest, rows shifted by k:")
print(shifts.round(3).to_string())
print("subjects where the unshifted rows give the highest fraction:", int((shifts.idxmax(axis=1) == 0).sum()), "of 12")
n_ok = int((link.matched & res_link.beats_all_shuffles).sum())
print("subjects with rows = electrodes and positions fitting the weights:", n_ok, "of 12")

Result: reproduced. The paper's code rule (keep the non-zero rows, drop the first) leaves as many rows as electrodes with a position in all 12 subjects; the dropped first row is the electrode density of each region, and the regions whose mean density exceeds 3 are exactly the eight of the claims file. After the density row, the zero rows of S03 (16) and S12 (8) sit exactly at the indices of the electrodes without a position, and the 4 extra zero rows of S01 come after its last electrode. For every subject the largest-weight region is the nearest region centroid for 36 to 55% of electrodes, against at most 14 electrodes in 200 shuffles of the electrode order, under all five seeds, and shifting the rows by 1 to 3 places lowers that fraction in all 12 subjects.

Spectral power of every event (streamed)¶

For each file, the chunk index of the ECoG series is read from the file's B-tree, and the chunks holding the 10 s around each event are fetched and decoded. The helper's docstring gives the source of every parameter. Every event's segment is checked by the Methods' rule, and its power is projected to the eight regions with the weights of the electrodes good in every file of the subject; the weights of each file's own good electrodes are kept as a variant. An electrode whose power is not finite in an event gets weight 0 in that event, and the region's weights are renormalised.

In [8]:
# SPECTRAL
t = time.time()
roi_idx = [cols_all.index(r) for r in ajile.ROIS]
# Electrodes good in every file of the subject (main). Variants, projection only: each file's own
# flags ("file"); the electrodes good in at least one file, i.e. only those bad in every file removed
# ("any"); and the main set with the electrodes holding a 50 ms run of zeros in an event dropped from
# that event ("zero_run", made in the helper).
GOOD_ALL = {s: np.all([m["electrodes"].good.values.astype(bool) for m in metas if int(m["subject_id"]) == s], axis=0)
            for s in subjects}
GOOD_ANY = {s: np.any([m["electrodes"].good.values.astype(bool) for m in metas if int(m["subject_id"]) == s], axis=0)
            for s in subjects}
W_MAIN = {s: ajile.session_weights(proj[s][1][:, roi_idx], GOOD_ALL[s]) for s in subjects}
W_ANY = {s: ajile.session_weights(proj[s][1][:, roi_idx], GOOD_ANY[s]) for s in subjects}
jobs = []
for m in metas:
    s = int(m["subject_id"])
    w_file = ajile.session_weights(proj[s][1][:, roi_idx], m["electrodes"].good.values.astype(bool))
    jobs.append((m["asset_id"], m["event_times"], GOOD_ALL[s], W_MAIN[s], {"file": w_file, "any": W_ANY[s]}))
spec = ajile.run_spectral(jobs, workers=8)
print(f"spectral pass {time.time() - t:.0f} s; peak memory of a worker "
      f"{resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss / 1e6:.2f} GB")

ev = ev_all.copy()
ev["inside"] = np.concatenate([r["inside"] for r in spec])
ev["allzero"] = np.concatenate([r["allzero"] for r in spec])
ev["seg_db"] = np.concatenate([r["seg_db"] for r in spec])
ev["hf_db"] = np.concatenate([r["hf_db"] for r in spec])
ev["n_dropped"] = np.concatenate([r["n_dropped"] for r in spec])
ev["n_zero_el"] = np.concatenate([r["n_zero_el"] for r in spec])
ev["n_zero_run"] = np.concatenate([r["n_zero_run"] for r in spec])
ev["event_time"] = np.concatenate([m["event_times"] for m in metas])
REG = np.concatenate([r["region"] for r in spec])          # (event, region, freq, bin), dB, no baseline
REG_BS = REG - REG[..., ajile.BASE].mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
REG_VAR = {k: np.concatenate([r["region_var"][k] for r in spec]) for k in spec[0]["region_var"]}  # variants
for r in spec:
    r["region"] = r["region_var"] = None
ELEC = {k: [r["elec"][k] for r in spec] for k in spec[0]["elec"]}  # per file: (event, electrode)
hf_thr = ev[ev.inside & ev.hf_db.notna()].groupby("subject").hf_db.agg(lambda x: x.mean() + 3 * x.std())
ev["hf_bad"] = ev.hf_db > ev.subject.map(hf_thr)
ev["low_power"] = ev.seg_db < 0
# Segments holding NaN samples (the files store missing ECoG as NaN) have NaN power: missing data
ev["nan_data"] = ev.inside & ev.seg_db.isna()
# The ECoG and pose windows use the ReachEvents time, the features the reaches table's start_time;
# an event where they disagree (data check) cannot be placed, and counts as missing data.
ev["time_mismatch"] = (ev.event_time - ev.start_time).abs() > 1
ev["keep"] = ev.inside & ~ev.nan_data & ~ev.allzero & ~ev.low_power & ~ev.hf_bad & ~ev.time_mismatch
drop = ev.groupby("subject").agg(events=("keep", "size"), no_ecog=("inside", lambda x: int((~x).sum())),
                                 time_mismatch=("time_mismatch", "sum"),
                                 nan_data=("nan_data", "sum"), zeroed=("allzero", "sum"), below_0dB=("low_power", "sum"),

# Clock check: event-locked band power at the true onsets against a pseudo-onset 3 s earlier in the
# same segments (same electrodes, same events). Precentral-weighted mean over the subject's good electrodes.
rows = []
for s in subjects:
    lf, hf, lfs, hfs = [], [], [], []
    for m, r in zip(metas, spec):
        if int(m["subject_id"]) != s:
            continue
        k = ev[(ev.asset_id == m["asset_id"])].keep.values
        w = np.nan_to_num(W_MAIN[s][:, 1])
        for key, lst in (("lfb_mean", lf), ("hfb_mean", hf), ("lfb_mean_shift", lfs), ("hfb_mean_shift", hfs)):
            lst.append(np.nansum(r["elec"][key][k] * w[None, :], axis=1))
    lf, hf, lfs, hfs = map(np.concatenate, (lf, hf, lfs, hfs))
    rows.append(dict(subject=s, lfb_onset=np.median(lf), lfb_pseudo=np.median(lfs),
                     hfb_onset=np.median(hf), hfb_pseudo=np.median(hfs),
                     p_hfb=stats.wilcoxon(hf, hfs).pvalue, p_lfb=stats.wilcoxon(lf, lfs).pvalue))
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(clock.round(4).to_string())

# Reach angle convention: the stored angle against the angle of the wrist's largest displacement
# from its onset position, computed from the pose (events up to 1.5 s long, the pose window)
W = np.concatenate([r["wrist"]["R_Wrist" if m["event_wrist"] == "r_wrist" else "L_Wrist"] for m, r in zip(metas, spec)])
img_ang, pmag = np.full(len(ev), np.nan), np.full(len(ev), np.nan)
for i in range(len(ev)):
    if ev.duration.values[i] > 1.5:
        continue
    n = int(ev.duration.values[i] * 30)
    seg = W[i, 45:46 + n] - W[i, 45]
    d = np.hypot(seg[:, 0], seg[:, 1])
    if np.isfinite(d).any():
        j = np.nanargmax(d)
        img_ang[i] = np.degrees(np.arctan2(seg[j, 1], seg[j, 0]))
        pmag[i] = d[j]
ok = np.isfinite(img_ang)
adiff = lambda a, b: np.abs((a - b + 180) % 360 - 180)
print("events compared:", ok.sum())
print("median |stored - image angle (y down)|:", np.median(adiff(ev.angle_raw.values[ok], img_ang[ok])).round(2), "deg")
print("median |stored - angle with y up|:", np.median(adiff(ev.angle_raw.values[ok], -img_ang[ok])).round(2), "deg")
print("median pose magnitude / stored magnitude:", np.median(pmag[ok] / ev.magnitude.values[ok]).round(3))

Event sets¶

Reading (a): every event in the reaches tables. Reading (b): the events left after the Methods' segment rejection (no ECoG for the whole 10 s segment, zeroed data, power below 0 dB, or 115-125 Hz power more than 3 SD above the subject's segments), and the one event whose ReachEvents time and reaches start_time disagree (data check). The dataset has no false-positive flag; the Methods say those events were removed by visual inspection, so none are dropped for it here.

cohort¶

Twelve subjects (8 male, 4 female, 29.4 +- 7.9 years) had on average 87.0 +- 12.9 surface electrodes; five also had 23.2 +- 12.1 depth electrodes; five were implanted in the right hemisphere and seven in the left.

Surface electrodes are those of groups whose description is not a depth electrode; depth electrodes are those of groups described as depth. The hemisphere is the side of the mean x (MNI) of the subject's electrodes with positions.

Result: partially reproduced. Twelve subjects, 8 male, mean age 29.42 years (SD 7.94), 84.83 surface electrodes on average and 5 right-hemisphere implants match. Electrode groups described as depth are in 7 subjects, not 5 (S01, S02, S03, S09, S10, S11, S12), with 23.71 depth electrodes on average, within the stated SD of 23.2. Counting only the grid as surface gives 63.08 electrodes on average, outside 87.0 +- 12.9, so the group descriptions are the reading kept.

Result: not reproduced. Under no reading are all three values within tolerance. All events: 211 to 996, median 770.5. After the segment rejection: 210 to 976, median 692.0. Events with ECoG and no missing samples: 211 to 986, median 700.5. The paper gives 151 to 947, median 640; the fewest events are 210 or more in every reading, outside 151 +- 15.1. Keeping only events of 0.5 to 4 s (the Methods' filter, not a reading of the criterion) still leaves at least 207 per subject.

fig2-features-differ-across-subjects¶

All ten behavioural and environmental features differ significantly across subjects.

def kw_by_subject(E):
    out = {}
    for f in ajile.FEATURES:
        groups = [g[f].values for _, g in E.groupby("subject")]
        out[f] = stats.kruskal(*groups)
    return pd.DataFrame({f: dict(H=r.statistic, p=r.pvalue) for f, r in out.items()}).T

fig2-reach-shape¶

Reach duration and reach magnitude vary little across subjects, with most reaches lasting under 2 s and covering under 200 pixels, and reach angle distributions tend to be bimodal with peaks near +90 and -90 degrees, with few side-to-side reaches.

Angle density: Gaussian KDE with Scott's bandwidth on the folded angle, evaluated on -90 to 90 in steps of 0.5 degrees (a standard grid). The grid's end points count as local maxima when they exceed their neighbour, since the folded angle cannot pass +-90 (standard choice, stated).

In [17]:
grid = np.arange(-90, 90.01, 0.5)
def bimodal(a):
    d = stats.gaussian_kde(a)(grid)
    peaks = [i for i in range(len(d)) if (i == 0 or d[i] > d[i - 1]) and (i == len(d) - 1 or d[i] > d[i + 1])]
    top = sorted(peaks, key=lambda i: -d[i])[:2]
    pk = sorted(grid[top])
    d0 = d[np.argmin(np.abs(grid))]
    ok = len(pk) == 2 and abs(pk[0] + 90) <= 15 and abs(pk[1] - 90) <= 15 and d0 < min(d[top])
    return ok, pk, d0, [d[i] for i in top]
rows = []
for s, g in list(EVB.groupby("subject")) + [("pooled", EVB)]:
    ok, pk, d0, dp = bimodal(g.angle.values)
    rows.append(dict(subject=s, n=len(g), frac_dur_lt2=(g.duration < 2).mean(), median_dur=g.duration.median(),
                     frac_mag_lt200=(g.magnitude < 200).mean(), median_mag=g.magnitude.median(),
                     peaks=np.round(pk, 1), dens0=round(d0, 5), dens_peaks=np.round(dp, 5), bimodal_pm90=ok,
                     frac_side=(np.abs(g.angle) < 30).mean()))
rs = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(rs.to_string())
per = rs[rs.subject != "pooled"]; pool = rs[rs.subject == "pooled"].iloc[0]
dur_part = pool.frac_dur_lt2 > 0.5 and (per.frac_dur_lt2 > 0.5).sum() >= 10
mag_part = pool.frac_mag_lt200 > 0.5 and (per.frac_mag_lt200 > 0.5).sum() >= 10
ang_part = pool.bimodal_pm90 and per.bimodal_pm90.sum() > 6
print("duration part:", dur_part, (per.frac_dur_lt2 > 0.5).sum(), "of 12; magnitude part:", mag_part,
      (per.frac_mag_lt200 > 0.5).sum(), "of 12; angle part:", ang_part, per.bimodal_pm90.sum(), "of 12")
print("ranges: duration", EVB.duration.min().round(3), "to", EVB.duration.max().round(3), "s; magnitude",
      EVB.magnitude.min().round(1), "to", EVB.magnitude.max().round(1), "px")

                   for x in (-90, -75, 0, 75, 90)}, index=[f"S{s:02d}" for s in subjects] + ["pooled"])

Result: partially reproduced. Most reaches last under 2 s (88 to 95% per subject, 91.8% pooled) and cover under 200 pixels (59 to 100% per subject, 91.3% pooled), in all 12 subjects. The angle part fails: the density of the folded angle has its two highest maxima within 15 degrees of -90 and +90 with a lower density at 0 in none of the 12 subjects and not pooled. Pooled, the maxima are at -71.5 and +75 degrees, and the density at 0 (0.00407) is above the lower maximum (0.004). The density at +75 degrees is above that at +90 in every subject, which the kernel's smoothing at the boundary can cause; but only 6.4% of events lie within 15 degrees of -90 (19.7% of +90), and pooled the density at -75 degrees (0.00395) is below that at 0. Reading (a) gives the same outcome.

extfig2-1c-contralateral-larger¶

Across all 12 subjects, the median displacement of the contralateral wrist after movement onset is substantially greater than that of the ipsilateral wrist.

Contralateral wrist: the wrist named in the ReachEvents description of each file. Pose windows -1.5 to +1.5 s at 30 Hz; peak over 0 to 1.5 s of the median over events.

In [20]:
tw = spec[0]["wrist_t"]
contra, ipsi = [], []
for m, r in zip(metas, spec):
    c = "R_Wrist" if m["event_wrist"] == "r_wrist" else "L_Wrist"
    i = "L_Wrist" if c == "R_Wrist" else "R_Wrist"
    contra.append(r["wrist"][c]); ipsi.append(r["wrist"][i])
contra, ipsi = np.concatenate(contra), np.concatenate(ipsi)
base = (tw >= -1.5) & (tw <= -1.0); post = (tw >= 0) & (tw <= 1.5); onset = np.argmin(np.abs(tw))
def disp(P, reading):
    ref = np.nanmean(P[:, base], axis=1) if reading == "a" else P[:, onset]
    return np.linalg.norm(P - ref[:, None, :], axis=2)
rows = []
kb = ev.keep.values
for reading in ("a", "b"):
    Dc, Di = disp(contra, reading), disp(ipsi, reading)
    for s in subjects:

        mc, mi = np.nanmedian(Dc[sel], axis=0), np.nanmedian(Di[sel], axis=0)
        rows.append(dict(reading=reading, subject=s, n=int(sel.sum()), contra_peak=np.nanmax(mc[post]),
                         ipsi_peak=np.nanmax(mi[post]), ratio=np.nanmax(mc[post]) / np.nanmax(mi[post])))
dd = pd.DataFrame(rows)
dd["holds"] = dd.contra_peak > dd.ipsi_peak
print(dd.round(3).to_string())
print(dd.groupby("reading").holds.sum())
print("events with missing pose in the window:", int(np.isnan(contra[kb]).any(axis=(1, 2)).sum()), "of", int(kb.sum()))

fig3-group-lfb-decrease-hfb-increase¶

At the group level, low-frequency power decreases and high-frequency power increases at movement initiation in several cortical regions.

Per subject, the median over events (reading b) of baseline-subtracted region power; the mean over the 12 subjects; the group mean over -1.5 to -1 s subtracted again. Masking as in the code's tfr_boot_sig_mask as the claims file gives it: each subject's baseline bins are drawn at random within frequency, the median over subjects taken, about 2000 values per frequency; two-sided percentile p; Benjamini-Hochberg over the region's frequency and time bins (-1.5 to +1.0 s, the bins computed here); non-significant values set to 0.

In [23]:
kbv = ev.keep.values
subj_v = ev.subject.values
SUBJ_MED = np.stack([np.nanmedian(REG_BS[kbv & (subj_v == s)], axis=0) for s in subjects])  # (subj, roi, f, b)
GROUP = SUBJ_MED.mean(axis=0)
GROUP = GROUP - GROUP[..., ajile.BASE].mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
base_idx = np.flatnonzero(ajile.BASE)

def bh(p, q=0.05):
    p = p.ravel(); n = len(p); o = np.argsort(p)
    thr = q * np.arange(1, n + 1) / n
    ok = p[o] <= thr
    k = np.max(np.flatnonzero(ok)) + 1 if ok.any() else 0
    sig = np.zeros(n, bool); sig[o[:k]] = True
    return sig

def mask_group(rng, n_boot=2000, group=None, subj_med=None):
    group = GROUP if group is None else group
    subj_med = SUBJ_MED if subj_med is None else subj_med
    masked = np.zeros_like(group)
    for r in range(group.shape[0]):
        S = subj_med[:, r]                                   # (subj, f, b)
        null = np.empty((n_boot, S.shape[1]))
        for f in range(S.shape[1]):
            pick = rng.integers(0, len(base_idx), size=(n_boot, S.shape[0]))
            vals = S[np.arange(S.shape[0])[None, :], f, base_idx[pick]]
            null[:, f] = np.median(vals, axis=1)
        obs = group[r]
        p = np.empty_like(obs)
        for f in range(obs.shape[0]):
            for b in range(obs.shape[1]):
                p[f, b] = min(1.0, 2 * min((null[:, f] >= obs[f, b]).mean(), (null[:, f] <= obs[f, b]).mean()))
        sig = bh(p).reshape(obs.shape)
        masked[r] = np.where(sig, obs, 0.0)
    return masked

LOW = (ajile.FREQS >= 4) & (ajile.FREQS <= 30); HIGH = (ajile.FREQS >= 50) & (ajile.FREQS <= 120)
b0 = np.argmin(np.abs(ajile.BIN_T))
def fig3_outcome(M):
    rows = []
    for r, name in enumerate(ajile.ROI_NAMES):
        rows.append(dict(region=name, low_a=M[r][LOW][:, ajile.WIN].mean(), high_a=M[r][HIGH][:, ajile.WIN].mean(),
                         low_b=M[r][LOW][:, b0].mean(), high_b=M[r][HIGH][:, b0].mean()))
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("region")
    t["holds_a"] = (t.low_a < 0) & (t.high_a > 0); t["holds_b"] = (t.low_b < 0) & (t.high_b > 0)
    return t

Result: reproduced. In precentral, postcentral and inferior parietal regions the masked group power over 4-30 Hz is below 0 and over 50-120 Hz above 0, both over 0 to 0.5 s (for example precentral -0.728 and 0.411 dB) and at the bin of 0 s, under all five seeds. Middle frontal shows the same pattern; in supramarginal and the temporal regions the masked high-frequency values are at most 0.008 dB. All three named regions hold too under each of the three electrode variants (section below): each file's own flags, removing only the electrodes bad in every file, and leaving out the electrodes with 50 ms runs of zeros.

fig3-sensorimotor-largest¶

Spectral power changes are largest in precentral, postcentral and inferior parietal regions, and the three temporal regions show minimal movement-related changes.

temporal = ["superior temporal", "middle temporal", "inferior temporal"]
def largest(M):
    win_c = (ajile.BIN_T >= -0.5) & (ajile.BIN_T <= 0.5)
    t = pd.DataFrame({"a_all_0_0.5": [np.abs(M[r][:, ajile.WIN]).mean() for r in range(8)],
                      "b_low": [np.abs(M[r][LOW][:, ajile.WIN]).mean() for r in range(8)],
                      "b_high": [np.abs(M[r][HIGH][:, ajile.WIN]).mean() for r in range(8)],
                      "c_all_-0.5_0.5": [np.abs(M[r][:, win_c]).mean() for r in range(8)]}, index=ajile.ROI_NAMES)
    res = {}
    for col in ["a_all_0_0.5", "c_all_-0.5_0.5"]:
        top3 = t[col].sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3].tolist()
        res[col] = (sorted(top3) == sorted(named3), sum(n in top3 for n in named3),
                    all(t.loc[x, col] < t.loc[named3, col].min() for x in temporal), top3)
    # (b): a region ranks high when it is in the top three in both ranges
    tl = t.b_low.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3].tolist(); th = t.b_high.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:3].tolist()
    both = [n for n in named3 if n in tl and n in th]
    tmp_ok = all(t.loc[x, "b_low"] < t.loc[named3, "b_low"].min() and t.loc[x, "b_high"] < t.loc[named3, "b_high"].min() for x in temporal)
    res["b"] = (len(both) == 3, len(both), tmp_ok, (tl, th))
    return t, res

fig3-lfb-more-widespread¶

Low-frequency power decreases are more spatially widespread than high-frequency increases and are also present in supramarginal and superior temporal regions.

In [26]:
def widespread(M):
    neg = np.array([(M[r][LOW][:, ajile.WIN] < 0).sum() for r in range(8)])
    pos = np.array([(M[r][HIGH][:, ajile.WIN] > 0).sum() for r in range(8)])
    a_ = ((neg > 0).sum(), (pos > 0).sum())
    b_ = (neg.sum() / LOW.sum(), pos.sum() / HIGH.sum())
    present = {n: int(neg[ajile.ROI_NAMES.index(n)]) for n in ["supramarginal", "superior temporal"]}
    return neg, pos, a_, b_, present

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The readings disagree. Reading (b), bins per frequency bin, gives 36.0 significant negative low-frequency bins against 22.2 positive high-frequency bins, and holds under all five seeds. Reading (a), regions with any significant bin, gives 8 against 8 (not larger), and 7 or 8 against 8 under the other seeds. Supramarginal (30 bins) and superior temporal (27 bins) do have significant low-frequency decreases. The electrode variants (section below) give the same disagreement: 7 against 8 and 34.6 against 24.0 with each file's flags, 8 against 8 and 35.0 against 25.2 removing only the electrodes bad in every file, 8 against 8 and 36.6 against 22.1 without the zero-run electrodes.

fig4-precentral-subject-variability¶

In the precentral region every subject shows the low/high-frequency pattern, but amplitudes and frequency bands vary; subjects 03, 06, 07, 08 and 11 have increases up to 120 Hz, subjects 09 and 12 mainly at 60-80 Hz, and subjects 04 and 08 have narrower low-frequency decreases.

In [27]:
def fig4_parts(subj_med, show=True):
    out = print if show else (lambda *a, **k: None)
    P = subj_med[:, 1].copy()                                     # precentral (subj, f, b), unmasked
    P = P - P[..., ajile.BASE].mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    spec4 = P[..., ajile.WIN].mean(axis=-1)                        # (subj, f)
    F = ajile.FREQS
    tab4 = pd.DataFrame(spec4, index=[f"S{s:02d}" for s in subjects], columns=[int(f) for f in F])
    out(tab4.round(2).to_string())
    p1 = pd.DataFrame({"lfb_8_32": spec4[:, ajile.LFB].mean(1), "hfb_76_100": spec4[:, ajile.HFB].mean(1)}, index=tab4.index)
    p1["holds"] = (p1.lfb_8_32 < 0) & (p1.hfb_76_100 > 0)
    out(p1.round(3).to_string())
    part1 = bool(p1.holds.all())
    i116, i121 = list(F).index(116), list(F).index(121)
    part2_rows = {s: (spec4[subjects.index(s), i116] > 0 and spec4[subjects.index(s), i121] > 0) for s in [3, 6, 7, 8, 11]}
    part2 = all(part2_rows.values())
    hi = F >= 56
    p3 = {}
    for s in [9, 12]:
        v = spec4[subjects.index(s)]
        fmax = F[hi][np.argmax(v[hi])]; top = v[hi].max()
        p3[s] = (fmax, round(float(top), 3), round(float(v[(F >= 101)].mean()), 3), 61 <= fmax <= 76 and v[F >= 101].mean() < top / 2)
    part3 = all(x[3] for x in p3.values())
    low = F <= 46
    width = {s: int((spec4[i][low] < spec4[i][low].min() / 2).sum()) for i, s in enumerate(subjects)}
    fewest = sorted(width, key=lambda s: width[s])[:3]
    ties = sorted(width.values())[:4]
    part4 = 4 in fewest and 8 in fewest
    out("part 1 (every subject):", part1, "; part 2:", part2_rows, part2, "; part 3:", p3, part3)
    out("part 4 widths (bins below half the minimum, 1-46 Hz):", width, "; three fewest:", fewest, "(four smallest widths:", ties, ")", part4)
    out("parts holding:", sum([part1, part2, part3, part4]), "of 4")
    return [part1, part2, part3, part4], p1, width
parts4, p1, width = fig4_parts(SUBJ_MED)

Result: partially reproduced. Two of four parts hold. Part 2: S03, S06, S07, S08 and S11 have positive power at 116 and 121 Hz. Part 3: S09 and S12 peak at 76 and 66 Hz with means over 101-121 Hz below half the peak. Part 4 fails: the narrowest low-frequency decreases are S07 and S09 (2 bins), and S04 and S08 are among six subjects tied at 3 bins, so they are not among the three fewest. Part 1 fails in one subject: S09 has a mean of -0.039 dB over 76-100 Hz. The electrode variants (section below) give: with each file's own flags parts 2 to 4 hold (S04, S07 and S08 at 2 bins) and part 1 fails for S09 only (-0.030 dB), partially reproduced; removing only the electrodes bad in every file all four parts hold, which would be reproduced; without the zero-run electrodes two parts hold, and S09 still has a negative mean over 76-100 Hz (-0.029 dB), so its 50 ms runs of zeros do not explain its failure of part 1. The paper's count of removed electrodes favours each file's flags (section below), which give the same outcome as the main analysis.

Result: reproduced. Precentral band power differs across the 12 subjects in both bands, for band means and band medians (Kruskal-Wallis H = 740 to 1028, p below the smallest double), and under every electrode variant (band mean H = 740 to 1089, section below).

table1-subject-band-power-ci¶

Each subject's precentral band power lies in the 95% bootstrap interval Table 1 gives; LFB power is below baseline and HFB power above it for most subjects.

      7: ((-0.84, -0.51), (1.14, 1.34)), 8: ((-0.3, 0.04), (0.36, 0.63)), 9: ((-0.57, -0.08), (-0.11, 0.23)),

rng = np.random.default_rng(seed("table1-subject-band-power-ci"))
rows = []
for s, g in EVB.groupby("subject"):
    for bi, band in enumerate(("lfb", "hfb")):
        lo, hi_ = T1[s][bi]
        row = dict(subject=s, band=band, paper_lo=lo, paper_hi=hi_)
        for bst in ("mean", "median"):
            x = g[f"pre_{band}_{bst}"].values
            for stat, fn in (("mean", np.mean), ("median", np.median)):
                v = fn(x)
                row[f"{stat}_of_band{bst}"] = v
                row[f"in_{stat}_of_band{bst}"] = lo <= v <= hi_
            boot = np.array([np.median(x[rng.integers(0, len(x), len(x))]) for _ in range(5000)])
            row[f"ci_median_band{bst}"] = np.round(np.percentile(boot, [2.5, 97.5]), 2)
        rows.append(row)
t1 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(t1.round(3).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. Under the best reading (median over events of the band median), 18 of 24 subject and band values lie in Table 1's intervals; the other readings give 14, 16 and 16. Outside are S02 LFB (-0.103 against -1.12 to -0.31), S03 LFB (-1.584 against -2.11 to -1.73), S03 HFB (1.044 against 1.39 to 1.67), S06 LFB (-0.647 against -1.63 to -1.11), S06 HFB (1.874 against 2.02 to 2.37) and S10 LFB (-0.196 against -0.87 to -0.35). The median band mean is below 0 for LFB in 12 of 12 subjects and above 0 for HFB in 11 of 12. The electrode variants (section below) give at best 21 of 24 (each file's flags, mean of the band mean), 22 of 24 (removing only the electrodes bad in every file, mean of the band mean) and 18 of 24 (without the zero-run electrodes, median of the band median), partially reproduced in each.

fig5-recording-day-effects¶

Precentral band power differs significantly across recording days in LFB for subjects 03, 05, 06, 07, 08 and 11, and in HFB for subjects 03, 04, 07, 08 and 10, despite baseline subtraction.

In [31]:
paper_sig = {"lfb": {3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11}, "hfb": {3, 4, 7, 8, 10}}
rows = []
for s, g in EVB.groupby("subject"):
    for band in ("lfb", "hfb"):
        row = dict(subject=s, band=band, paper_sig=s in paper_sig[band])
        for bst in ("mean", "median"):
            p = stats.kruskal(*[x[f"pre_{band}_{bst}"].values for _, x in g.groupby("day")]).pvalue
            row[f"p_band{bst}"] = p; row[f"agree_band{bst}"] = (p < 0.05) == (s in paper_sig[band])
        row["day_means"] = np.round(g.groupby("day")[f"pre_{band}_mean"].mean().values, 2)
        rows.append(row)
t5 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(t5.to_string(float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.3g}"))

Result: partially reproduced, resting on the choice of good electrodes. With each file's own good-electrode flags, the choice closest to the paper's count of removed electrodes, 20 of 24 subject and band pairs agree with the paper with band means, the criterion's threshold for a partial reproduction, and 19 with band medians (section "Region results under other electrode choices"). With band means a day effect is found where the paper finds none for S01 LFB (p = 0.047), S01 HFB (p = 0.023) and S06 HFB (p = 6.7e-11), and is not found for S10 HFB (p = 0.094), where the paper finds one.

With the main set of this notebook (the table above) 18 of 24 pairs agree under both band statistics, below the 20 the criterion asks: S07 HFB (p = 0.073) and S08 LFB (p = 0.31) also lose their day effect, and S10 HFB has p = 0.054. Removing only the electrodes bad in every file gives 21 and 20 (S10 HFB p = 0.015). Leaving out the electrodes with 50 ms runs of zeros gives 18 and 18; S10 HFB keeps p = 0.054 under it, so the zeros do not explain that pair. The paper removes 4.9 +- 4.9 surface electrodes per subject; each file's flags remove 4.2 +- 2.1, the main set 12.6 +- 8.4 and removing only the electrodes bad in every file 1.2 +- 0.4 (data check). Each file's flags change the electrodes from day to day, which can add or hide day effects. The day medians of the band mean lie inside Table 2's per-day intervals for 41 of 55 subject-days in LFB and 42 of 55 in HFB. Not reproduced was the outcome verified in round 2; partially reproduced was proposed after it, and the round-3 verifier agreed.

extfig5-1-baseline-reduces-day-variability¶

Subtracting the -1.5 to -1 s baseline reduces the variability of band power across recording days, though clear variability remains.

Result: reproduced. Baseline subtraction lowers the SD of day means in 10 of 12 subjects for LFB and 12 of 12 for HFB (reading a), and at 91.3% and 90.2% of electrodes (reading b). Variability remains: day effects are significant in 11 subject and band pairs (fig5-recording-day-effects), with SDs of 0.03 to 0.83 dB after subtraction.

discussion-day-changes-small¶

Day-to-day changes in baseline-subtracted spectral power are small (about 1-2 dB) compared with spectral power without baseline subtraction (about 10-50 dB).

Result: reproduced. The largest deviation of a day mean from the subject mean is 1.49 dB (S06 HFB), at most 2.2 dB in every subject and band (1.49 dB under each electrode variant too). Without baseline subtraction the precentral band power is 11.7 to 36.9 dB in microvolts squared, within 9 to 55 dB; in volts squared it would be about -108 to -83 dB.

Region results under other electrode choices (variants)¶

The main analysis projects every event with the electrodes good in every file of the subject (the claims file's opening comment: bad electrodes get weight 0 and the weights are renormalised per subject). Here the region claims are recomputed, on the same events, with (1) the flags of each event's own file, the assumption of the first round of this attempt; (2) the electrodes good in at least one file of the subject, that is, removing only the electrodes bad in every file, which is also per subject, keeps the electrodes the same across days and removes the fewest electrodes (data check); and (3) the main set with, in each event, the electrodes holding a run of at least 50 ms of exact zeros left out. The bootstrap masks use the generator of claim fig3-group-lfb-decrease-hfb-increase plus 1, 2 and 3. For fig5-recording-day-effects every pair's p is printed.

In [34]:
VARIANTS = {"file": ("each file's own flags", 1), "any": ("removing only electrodes bad in every file", 2),
            "zero_run": ("main set without zero-run electrodes", 3)}
VAR_RES = {}
for key, (label, off) in VARIANTS.items():
    RB = REG_VAR[key] - REG_VAR[key][..., ajile.BASE].mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    SM = np.stack([np.nanmedian(RB[kbv & (subj_v == s)], axis=0) for s in subjects])
    GA = SM.mean(axis=0)
    GA = GA - GA[..., ajile.BASE].mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    MA = mask_group(np.random.default_rng(seed("fig3-group-lfb-decrease-hfb-increase") + off), group=GA, subj_med=SM)
    print(f"=== {label} ({key})")
    tA = fig3_outcome(MA)
    print("fig3-group: named regions holding under a:", int(tA.loc[named3, "holds_a"].sum()), "; under b:", int(tA.loc[named3, "holds_b"].sum()),
          {k: {r: round(float(v), 3) for r, v in d.items()} for k, d in tA.loc[named3, ["low_a", "high_a"]].to_dict().items()})
    _, rA = largest(MA)
    print("fig3-sensorimotor:", {k: (v[0], v[1], v[2]) for k, v in rA.items()})
    _, _, aA, bA, pA = widespread(MA)
    print("fig3-lfb-more-widespread: (a)", tuple(int(x) for x in aA), "; (b)", np.round(bA, 3), "; supramarginal / superior temporal:", pA)
    partsA, p1A, wA = fig4_parts(SM, show=False)
    print("fig4: parts holding", sum(partsA), "of 4", partsA, "; subjects without the part 1 pattern:", list(p1A.index[~p1A.holds]),
          p1A[~p1A.holds].round(3).to_dict("index"), "; part 4 widths:", {f"S{int(s):02d}": int(v) for s, v in wA.items()})
    stA = ajile.band_stats(RB[:, 1])
    EA = ev.copy()
    for k, v in stA.items():
        EA["pre_" + k] = v
    EA = EA[EA.keep]
    print("fig5-band-power: H (band mean) LFB", round(stats.kruskal(*[x.pre_lfb_mean.values for _, x in EA.groupby("subject")]).statistic, 1),
          "HFB", round(stats.kruskal(*[x.pre_hfb_mean.values for _, x in EA.groupby("subject")]).statistic, 1))
    inA = {f"{st}_of_band{bst}": 0 for st in ("mean", "median") for bst in ("mean", "median")}
    agA = {"mean": 0, "median": 0}; devA, prow = [], []
    for s, g in EA.groupby("subject"):
        for bi, band in enumerate(("lfb", "hfb")):
            lo, hi_ = T1[s][bi]
            for bst in ("mean", "median"):
                x = g[f"pre_{band}_{bst}"].values
                for st, fn in (("mean", np.mean), ("median", np.median)):
                    inA[f"{st}_of_band{bst}"] += lo <= fn(x) <= hi_
                p = stats.kruskal(*[x_[f"pre_{band}_{bst}"].values for _, x_ in g.groupby("day")]).pvalue
                agA[bst] += (p < 0.05) == (s in paper_sig[band])
                prow.append(dict(subject=s, band=band, stat=bst, p=p, paper_sig=s in paper_sig[band], agree=(p < 0.05) == (s in paper_sig[band])))
            dm = g.groupby("day")[f"pre_{band}_mean"].mean()
            devA.append((dm - g[f"pre_{band}_mean"].mean()).abs().max())
    print("table1: inside, four readings", inA)
    print("fig5-recording-day-effects: pairs agreeing, band mean", agA["mean"], "of 24, band median", agA["median"], "of 24")
    pr = pd.DataFrame(prow)
    print("   pairs that disagree with the paper:", [(f"S{r.subject:02d}", r.band, r.stat, f"p={r.p:.3g}") for r in pr[~pr.agree].itertuples()])
    print("   S09 and S10, p (band mean):", {(f"S{r.subject:02d}", r.band): float(f"{r.p:.3g}") for r in pr[(pr.subject.isin([9, 10])) & (pr.stat == "mean")].itertuples()})
    print("discussion: largest day deviation", round(float(max(devA)), 3), "dB")
    VAR_RES[key] = dict(parts=partsA, inA=inA, agA=agA, pr=pr)
    del RB

Electrode choice, and the outcome of fig5-recording-day-effects. The Methods ("ECoG data processing") remove "4.9 +- 4.9 surface electrodes per subject and 1.0 +- 1.4 depth electrodes for each of the five subjects with depth electrodes". The data check counts the surface electrodes each choice removes: 12.6 +- 8.4 per subject for the main set (electrodes bad in any file removed), 4.2 +- 2.1 for each file's own flags (mean over a subject's files), and 1.2 +- 0.4 when only the electrodes bad in every file are removed. Each file's flags are closest to the paper's count. No choice matches the depth count (8.1, 4.7 and 3.1 against 1.0), mostly because S03's 16 depth electrodes, which have no position, are bad in every file.

Under each file's flags fig5-recording-day-effects has 20 of 24 pairs agreeing (band mean), and removing only the electrodes bad in every file gives 21; both are partially reproduced under the criterion. Each file's flags change the electrodes from day to day, which can add or hide day effects; removing only the electrodes bad in every file keeps them the same, as the main set does. Only the main set gives 18. The other region claims keep their outcomes under each file's flags (fig3 group pattern and sensorimotor regions reproduced, the widespread readings still disagree, fig4 three of four parts, band power differs across subjects, Table 1 21 of 24, day changes at most 1.49 dB). Removing only the electrodes bad in every file would make fig4 reproduced (four of four parts), but that choice removes far fewer electrodes than the paper reports. The regression claims were not refit under each file's flags. The outcome of fig5-recording-day-effects is partially reproduced, resting on each file's own flags as the choice best supported by the paper's count; it was proposed after round 2 and the round-3 verifier agreed.

Regression models (Figure 6)¶

One model per subject, electrode and band, on the events of reading (b). Electrodes are those good in every file of the subject (the Methods remove bad electrodes; the flags differ between files, see the data check). Ten features as the Methods and code encode them; forward selection over single columns on all events (code); Huber regression (sklearn defaults); 200 day-balanced splits with 10% test events (Methods), and 20% (code) as a variant. Delta R2 is computed where the model's own R2, or its electrode's LFB R2, exceeds 0.05. The splits use the generator of claim fig6b-best-models-sensorimotor, the 80/20 splits its seed + 1 and the shuffles its seed + 2; the other Figure 6 claims use these same fits. Forward selection on all events lets the test events of each split take part in choosing the features, as the code does and the claims file prescribes; this can raise R2 a little. After the claim sections, the models with R2 > 0.03 are refit under the four other seeds and with log(onset speed + 1), and the electrodes bad in at least one file are fit as the code does; Delta R2 and coefficients are recomputed for each.

t = time.time()
REG_SEED = seed("fig6b-best-models-sensorimotor")
def regression_jobs(seed0, include_bad=False, log_speed=False):
    jobs = []
    for s in subjects:
        idx = [i for i, m in enumerate(metas) if int(m["subject_id"]) == s]
        E = pd.concat([ev[ev.asset_id == metas[i]["asset_id"]] for i in idx])
        keep = E.keep.values
        G = np.array([metas[i]["electrodes"].good.values for i in idx])
        use = np.ones(G.shape[1], bool) if include_bad else G.all(axis=0)
        Y = np.stack([np.concatenate([ELEC[k][i] for i in idx])[keep][:, use]
                      for k in ("lfb_mean", "hfb_mean", "lfb_median", "hfb_median")], axis=-1)
        finite = np.isfinite(Y).all(axis=(0, 2))
        Ek = E[keep]
        X, names = ajile.design_matrix(Ek, log_speed=log_speed)
        jobs.append(dict(subject=s, X=X, names=names, Y=Y[:, finite], days=Ek.day.values, seed=seed0,
                         electrodes=np.flatnonzero(use)[finite], targets=["lfb_mean", "hfb_mean", "lfb_median", "hfb_median"],
                         main_targets=["lfb_mean", "hfb_mean"], delta_min_r2=0.05, dropped_nonfinite=int((~finite).sum()),
                         good_all=G.all(axis=0)))
    return jobs
JOBS = regression_jobs(REG_SEED)
print("models per subject (electrodes):", {j["subject"]: j["Y"].shape[1] for j in JOBS},
      "; electrodes dropped for non-finite power:", {j["subject"]: j["dropped_nonfinite"] for j in JOBS})
REGR = pd.DataFrame(ajile.run_regression(JOBS, workers=4))
print(f"regression {time.time() - t:.0f} s, {len(REGR)} models")
REGR["band"] = REGR.target.str[:3]
MAIN = REGR[REGR.target.isin(["lfb_mean", "hfb_mean"])].copy()
print(MAIN.groupby("band").r2.describe().round(4).to_string())
print("Huber fits that did not converge (main models, 200 fits each):", int(MAIN.nonconverged.sum()), "of", 200 * len(MAIN),
      "; models with any:", int((MAIN.nonconverged > 0).sum()))

sensor3 = ["precentral", "postcentral", "inferior parietal"]
def region_of(s, e):
    w = proj[s][1][e, roi_idx]
    return ajile.ROI_NAMES[int(np.argmax(w))] if w.sum() > 0 else "none"
MAIN["region"] = [region_of(s, e) for s, e in zip(MAIN.subject, MAIN.electrode)]
for band in ("lfb", "hfb"):
    M = MAIN[MAIN.band == band]
    sel = M[M.r2 > 0.05]
    frac = sel.region.isin(frontopar).mean() if len(sel) else np.nan
    med_s = M[M.region.isin(sensor3)].r2.median(); med_t = M[M.region.isin(temporal)].r2.median()
    # (b) projected R2: per subject weighted mean with the good-electrode weights, then mean over subjects
    proj_r2 = []
    for s in subjects:
        Ms = M[M.subject == s]
        w = np.nan_to_num(proj[s][1][Ms.electrode.values][:, roi_idx])
        w = w / np.where(w.sum(0) > 0, w.sum(0), np.nan)
        proj_r2.append(np.nansum(w * Ms.r2.values[:, None], axis=0))
    pr = pd.Series(np.nanmean(proj_r2, axis=0), index=ajile.ROI_NAMES).sort_values(ascending=False)
    print(f"{band.upper()}: (a) {len(sel)} models with R2 > 0.05, fraction in the five frontoparietal regions {frac:.3f};",
          f"median R2 sensorimotor {med_s:.4f} vs temporal {med_t:.4f}")
    print("   regions of the models with R2 > 0.05:", sel.region.value_counts().to_dict())
    print("   (b) projected R2 by region:", pr.round(4).to_dict(), "-> top three frontoparietal:", all(x in frontopar for x in pr.index[:3]))
    print("   models with R2 > 0.05 per subject:", sel.subject.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())

fig6c-angle-and-day-most-informative¶

Reach angle and day of recording are the most informative features for single-event power, especially for low-frequency power.

In [38]:
def delta_table(df, col="delta", select="own"):
    out = {}
    for band in ("lfb", "hfb"):
        M = df[df.band == band]
        if select == "own":
            M = M[M.r2 > 0.05]
        else:
            lfb_r2 = df[df.band == "lfb"].set_index(["subject", "electrode"]).r2
            M = M[[lfb_r2.get((s, e), -1) > 0.05 for s, e in zip(M.subject, M.electrode)]]
        D = pd.DataFrame([d for d in M[col] if isinstance(d, dict)])
        out[band] = D.median().sort_values(ascending=False) if len(D) else pd.Series(dtype=float)
        out[band + "_n"] = len(D)
    return out
for label, col, selm in (("Methods Delta R2, own-band selection", "delta", "own"),
                         ("code Delta R2 (80/20, test shuffled), own-band selection", "delta_code", "own"),
                         ("Methods Delta R2, selection by LFB R2 (code)", "delta", "lfb")):
    d = delta_table(MAIN, col, selm)
    print(label)
    for band in ("lfb", "hfb"):
        print(f"  {band.upper()} ({d[band + '_n']} models):", d[band].round(5).to_dict())
        print("     top two:", list(d[band].index[:2]))

Over the 14 LFB models with R2 > 0.05, recording day (median Delta R2 0.037) and reach angle (0.031) are the two most informative features; the other eight have medians of at most 0.0001. In HFB the same two lead (0.062 and 0.022), and under the code's Delta R2 and the code's selection by LFB R2 too (with that selection the HFB order is angle, then day). Under the four other seeds, with log(onset speed + 1) and with the bad electrodes included, the top two are day and angle in both bands.

Reach angle is the feature most often retained by forward selection in sensorimotor regions, followed by reach duration, reach magnitude, bimanual ratio and bimanual overlap.

In [39]:
RET = {}
for band in ("lfb", "hfb"):
    M = MAIN[MAIN.band == band]
    per_s = []
    for s in subjects:
        Ms = M[M.subject == s]
        R = pd.DataFrame(list(Ms.retention)).reindex(columns=ajile.FEATURES).values
        w = np.nan_to_num(proj[s][1][Ms.electrode.values][:, roi_idx])
        w = w / np.where(w.sum(0) > 0, w.sum(0), np.nan)
        per_s.append(np.einsum("er,ef->rf", np.nan_to_num(w), R))
    RET[band] = pd.DataFrame(np.nanmean(per_s, axis=0), index=ajile.ROI_NAMES, columns=ajile.FEATURES)
    print(band.upper()); print(RET[band].round(3).to_string())
angle_top = {(b, r): RET[b].loc[r].idxmax() for b in ("lfb", "hfb") for r in sensor3}

Result: partially reproduced. Reach angle is the most often retained feature in precentral, postcentral and inferior parietal regions for both bands (0.52 averaged over these). The order of the next four does not hold: over the sensorimotor regions it is magnitude (0.356), speech ratio (0.355), duration (0.354) and onset speed (0.350), and over all regions speech ratio, bimanual class, bimanual ratio and onset speed.

fig6d-upward-reaches-enhance-pattern¶

Upward reaches are associated with lower low-frequency power and higher high-frequency power.

    print(label, {b: dict(n=v[0], median_angle_coef=round(float(v[1]), 4), frac_negative=round(float(v[2]), 3)) for b, v in out.items()})

Result: reproduced. Under both readings, recording day (SD of its one-hot coefficients) and reach angle have the two largest coefficient magnitudes in both bands: LFB 0.97 and 0.71, HFB 0.71 and 0.53 (the next is magnitude, 0.28). The code's selection by LFB R2 gives the same two (HFB 0.24 and 0.23), and so do the four other seeds, log(onset speed + 1) and the bad electrodes included (reading a).

In [42]:
# Variants of the Figure 6 models. Each refits the models with R2 > 0.03 under the main fits (all
# models that pass 0.05 come from these), with the Methods' 90/10 splits and Delta R2 where R2 > 0.05.
def fig6_summary(df):
    """Per band: models with R2 > 0.05, the two features with the largest median Delta R2
    (fig6c), the median reach angle coefficient (fig6d-upward) and the two largest median
    coefficient magnitudes (fig6d-largest, reading a)."""
    out = {}
    for band in ("lfb", "hfb"):
        M = df[(df.band == band) & (df.r2 > 0.05)]
        D = pd.DataFrame([d for d in M.delta if isinstance(d, dict)]).median().sort_values(ascending=False)
        if len(M) == 0:
            out[band] = dict(n=0)
            continue
        Cf = pd.DataFrame(list(M.coef))
        ca = Cf.abs().median().sort_values(ascending=False)
        out[band] = dict(n=len(M), top_delta=list(D.index[:2]), angle_coef=round(float(Cf.angle.median()), 3),
                         top_coef=list(ca.index[:2]))
    return out
def variant_jobs(jobs0, models, **kw):
    jobs = []
    for j in jobs0:
        es = set(models[models.subject == j["subject"]].electrode)
        k = np.array([e in es for e in j["electrodes"]])
        if not k.any():
            continue
        jj = dict(j); jj["Y"] = j["Y"][:, k][:, :, :2]; jj["electrodes"] = j["electrodes"][k]
        jj["targets"] = ["lfb_mean", "hfb_mean"]; jj["variant"] = True
        jj.update(kw)
        jobs.append(jj)
    return jobs
print("main fits:", fig6_summary(MAIN))
# All variant fits run in one pool, largest jobs first; each job keeps its own generators, so this
# gives the same fits as running each variant on its own.
t = time.time()
top = MAIN[MAIN.r2 > 0.03][["subject", "electrode"]].drop_duplicates()
print("models refit per variant:", len(top), "electrodes, both bands")
# Seeds: the splits and shuffles of the claim's seed + 1000 ... + 4000
VJOBS = {f"seed + {off}": variant_jobs(JOBS, top, seed=REG_SEED + off) for off in SEED_OFFSETS[1:]}
# log(onset speed + 1) as the code encodes it (claims file, opening comment)
VJOBS["log"] = variant_jobs(regression_jobs(REG_SEED, log_speed=True), top)
# Bad electrodes included, as the code fits them (claims file, opening comment): the main fits plus
# the electrodes bad in at least one file of the subject
JOBS_BAD = regression_jobs(REG_SEED, include_bad=True)
extra = []
for j in JOBS_BAD:
    k = ~j["good_all"][j["electrodes"]]
    jj = dict(j); jj["Y"] = j["Y"][:, k][:, :, :2]; jj["electrodes"] = j["electrodes"][k]
    jj["targets"] = ["lfb_mean", "hfb_mean"]; jj["variant"] = True
    extra.append(jj)
VJOBS["bad"] = [j for j in extra if len(j["electrodes"])]
flat = [(key, j) for key, js in VJOBS.items() for j in js]
VR = {}
for (key, _), rows in zip(flat, ajile.run_regression([j for _, j in flat], workers=4, per_job=True)):
    VR.setdefault(key, []).extend(rows)
VR = {key: pd.DataFrame(rows).assign(band=lambda d: d.target.str[:3]) for key, rows in VR.items()}
print(f"variant fits {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
sens = {}
for off in SEED_OFFSETS[1:]:
    R = VR[f"seed + {off}"]
    sens[off] = R
    print(f"seed + {off}: largest R2 {R.r2.max():.4f};", fig6_summary(R))

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper started from its own curated epochs and spectral power (Figshare); here everything is computed from the dataset's continuous ECoG, with the Methods' spectral method and the code's parameters. The segment rejection pools power over the good electrodes and 1-200 Hz (an assumption). The good-electrode flags differ between a subject's files; the electrodes good in every file of the subject are used throughout (an assumption). For the region claims, each file's own flags, the electrodes good in at least one file, and the main set without electrodes holding 50 ms runs of zeros are shown as variants. The choice decides fig5-recording-day-effects (18 of 24 pairs agree with the main set, 20 with each file's flags, 21 with the electrodes good in at least one file), and the paper's count of removed surface electrodes (4.9 +- 4.9) is closest to each file's flags (4.2 +- 2.1, against 12.6 +- 8.4 for the main set), so that outcome rests on each file's flags and is partially reproduced. Removing only the electrodes bad in every file would also make fig4-precentral-subject-variability reproduced. The dataset has no false-positive flag, so none are removed beyond what it holds. The regression's Delta R2 is computed only where R2 > 0.05 (the only models the claims use), and the code's Delta R2 variant is run with the code's 80/20 splits. The seed, log(onset speed + 1) and bad-electrode variants refit the models with R2 > 0.03 under the main fits, and the bad electrodes, with the Methods' splits.

What was found about the dataset (numbers above):

  • The subjects and days are those of the paper, and the paper's projection matrices match the electrodes in all 12 subjects. The event features, the pose and the ECoG agree with one another: the stored reach magnitude equals the one computed from the pose (ratio 1.007), and event-locked power changes at the true onsets differ from those at pseudo-onsets 3 s earlier (Wilcoxon p < 0.05) in 10 of 12 subjects for LFB and 8 of 12 for HFB. For S09 neither band differs, so the neural data could not establish the alignment there.
  • The ECoG of three files ends hours before the day ends (S01 day 7, S04 day 3, S06 day 3), while the pose and the events go on: 237 events have no ECoG. Another 125 events fall on NaN samples.
  • In S09 and S10 every analysed event has, on at least one electrode marked good in every file, a run of at least 25 exact zero samples (50 ms) in its 10 s segment; no electrode's wavelet power becomes infinite in the analysis window. Leaving those electrodes out of each event changes no outcome: S09 still has no HFB increase in the precentral region, S10's HFB day effect keeps p = 0.054, and S09's onset and pseudo-onset power still do not differ (p = 0.84 and 0.87).
  • The dataset holds more events than the paper analysed (8088; 211 to 996 per subject, median 770.5, against 151 to 947, median 640).
  • Undocumented conventions: the reach angle is in image coordinates (y down); the bimanual overlap, described as a fraction of the movement, is in seconds (1708 of all 8088 events above 1); the pose is labelled meters but is in pixels; good-electrode flags differ between a subject's files; 24 electrodes (S03, S12) have no position; the electrodes table carries R2 columns without a description.
  • One event (S08 day 4) is at 40.3 s in ReachEvents and at 86440.3 s in the reaches table, past the end of the 86400 s recording; it is left out of reading (b).
  • Electrode groups described as depth are in 7 subjects, where the paper reports 5.
